title: Response Path SLO Heatmap and Pager Classifier
creator: Aisha Morgan
description: Build a request-path focused SLO heatmap and an automated pager-classifier that combines tracing hooks, metric/log pipelines, and historic incident labels to: (1) surface which request paths drive SLO burn, (2) attach contextual traces/log snippets to burn-rate alerts, and (3) reduce noisy oncall pages by classifying and remediating low-actionability alerts. This ticket covers schema changes for trace hooks, ingest pipeline enrichments, dashboard UX, offline classifier training, and a staged rollout with canary/QA verification.
acceptance_criteria: SLO heatmap UI shows per-request-path latency percentiles (P50/P90/P95/P99) and error rates for any selected time-range with color-coded burn intensity.
Heatmap rows are backed by a new 'request_path' dimension emitted by tracing hooks and present in metrics/aggregations within 60s of production traffic.
Burn-rate alerts can be scoped to request_path with a template that auto-populates top contributing spans and last 3 trace IDs.
Pager classifier model achieves >=40% reduction in simulated noisy pages (precision >= 0.75 for 'no-action' label) on replay of last 12 months incident data.
Integration test: an injected synthetic latency spike for /api/v2/search should create a burn-rate alert scoped to that path and surface 3 sample traces directly from the alert UI.
Rollout: feature gate enabled for 10% of traffic for 3 days, 50% for 2 days, then full. Canary must show no increase in missed-critical pages and no regression in alert delivery latency.
Documentation: runbook and run-time query templates added to Confluence with links from alert UI; SDK changes documented in Developer Guide.
